header: THE SMALL PICTURE OF A NEWS CARD. The feeds give a picture for most English and Hindi stories (and the business papers'), but at the size of the papers' own pages: 1200 to 1600 pixels wide, 100 to 400 KB each, for a box that is 96 pixels wide on the card. Showing them as they are would put several megabytes on a screen of fifteen cards, which is the slowness the owner feared. So the browser never asks the paper for the picture: it asks THIS intranet's route /api/live/thumb, which fetches the picture once, makes it 360 x 240 pixels (3:2, the shape of the pictures of the Bengali news page the owner pointed to; twice the 180 x 120 box, for sharp screens; the picture is cropped to the shape, never stretched) as a WebP of 8 to 20 KB, and says that it may be kept for a day by the browser and a week by the host's shared cache: the first person to open a story's picture pays for the making (a fraction of a second, and the card's text is already on the screen), every later one gets 5 KB from the cache. The feed itself carries only the picture's address, so the news answer is no slower for it. This route fetches an address it was given, so it fetches ONLY from the hosts below (the image servers of the papers whose feeds I read), only over https, and nothing else: it cannot be used to reach an address inside a network or an arbitrary site. A host that is not in the list gives no picture and the card shows its tile.

symbols.name: MAX_SOURCE_BYTES
doc: The most bytes of a picture I will read (the papers' pictures are up to a few hundred KB).

symbols.name: IMAGE_HOSTS
doc: The image servers of the papers: a host is allowed when it is one of these or a subdomain of one.

symbols.name: ARTICLE_HOSTS
doc: The papers whose STORY PAGES I read when a list is built (src/lib/live/pageFacts.ts): to take the picture the paper itself attaches to the story (its og:image, the picture a link preview shows) when the feed carries none, and to see whether the paper marks the story as paid. These are the papers whose pages answer an ordinary request (checked 28 Nov 2026: Jagran, Amar Ujala, Bartaman, Aajkaal, Sangbad Pratidin, Ei Samay, each in 0.2 to 0.5 s). I do NOT read a paper that refuses automated requests (Anandabazar Patrika and The Telegraph answer 403 even for robots.txt): I do not work around a refusal, and their stories show Bing's picture of the story where Bing has it, and a tile where it has not.

symbols.name: isAllowedImage
doc: Is this an https address on one of the papers' image servers (no port, no login in it, no IP number)?

symbols.name: thumbSrc
symbols.sig: const thumbSrc = (image: string | undefined | null): string | null =>
doc: The address the card's uses for a story's picture (the picture's address was found when the list was built: in the feed, on the story's own page, or at Bing); null when the story has none or the route would refuse it, and the card then shows its tile at once, with no request.

symbols.name: smallerAddress
doc: Where a paper's image server lets the size be asked for in the address, I ask for a small one instead of fetching the big one and making it small here. Only Bhaskar needs it: most of its feed's pictures are animated GIFs, 1 to 7 MB at the 1000 x 1000 the feed names and 1 MB at 200 x 200 (measured 28 Nov 2026). The other papers' pictures are 40 to 500 KB and are fetched as given.

symbols.name: hostOk
symbols.sig: const hostOk = (raw: string, hosts: string[]): boolean =>

symbols.name: isReadableArticle
doc: Is this the page of a story of a paper whose pages I read (https, on its own host)?

symbols.name: MAX_PAGE_BYTES
doc: The most bytes of a story page I read: the picture's tag is in the head, in the first 100 to 200 KB, and I stop at the end of the head.

symbols.name: pictureOfPage
symbols.sig: export function pictureOfPage(html: string, pageUrl: string): string | null
doc: The picture a paper attaches to a story, from the story page's head: og:image (the one a link preview shows), else twitter:image. Returns the https address, or null. A relative address is made absolute against the page. Only what is in a <meta> tag is read: nothing in the page is run.

symbols.name: usableImage
doc: Can this picture become a thumbnail? The Times of India and Economic Times addresses carry the picture's size in bytes ("...,imgsize-17121652.cms"): one over the ceiling (an animated GIF of 17 MB was in the feed of 28 Nov 2026, and the paper's own resizing gave 26 MB) cannot be fetched, so the story has NO usable picture. Other addresses are taken as usable (the route refuses a file that turns out too large).

symbols.name: rejectPicture
doc: The owner's rule: no relevant picture, no story. A picture found to be a logo or a flat graphic (photoHash.ts looksLikeLogo: a paper's own logo that an image search gave for its story) is no picture: from now on usableImage says no to it.

behaviours: every picture address of the real feeds (the thirteen image servers of the papers that give pictures) is allowed

what is not on a paper's image server over plain https is refused: http, another site, a look-alike (toiimg.com.evil.example, evil-toiimg.com), an IP number (also the cloud's internal address), a login in the address, another port, file, javascript and data addresses
a sub-domain of a listed server is allowed, the bare domain too, and the list names real image servers only
the card asks the intranet's own route, with the address encoded; a picture the route would refuse, or none, gives no address (the card shows its tile at once)
the picture is made twice the box of the card (360 x 240, 3:2, for a box of 180 x 120), for sharp screens, and has the same shape as the box (so it is never stretched)
Bhaskar's server is asked for a 200 x 200 picture instead of the 1000 x 1000 animated GIF the feed names; other servers' addresses are not touched
Ei Samay's and Bing's picture servers are allowed (the Ei Samay sitemap's pictures; Bing's thumbnail of a story)

the story pages that are read are those of the papers whose pages answer an ordinary request; Anandabazar Patrika and The Telegraph (403 to every automated request) and Google News links are never read
the picture a paper attaches to a story is its og:image (else twitter:image), read from the page's meta tags, made absolute, made https; entities are decoded; a page without one gives none
a picture whose address says it is over the 6 MB ceiling (the Times of India's 17 MB animated GIF) is not usable; the ordinary ones, and addresses that say nothing of size, are
